author: Linnaeus, 1766
status: 겨울철새, 해마다 수천 마리 · 여름에도 드물게 기록(10건 미만)
summary: 겨울철새로, 철원, 연천, 파주 등지에서 흔히 볼 수 있고 요즘은 전국에서 관찰된다. 우리나라에 오는 수리류 가운데 가장 크다. 무리 지어 다니는 때가 많으며, 날갯짓을 거의 하지 않고 상승 기류를 타고 날면서 동물의 사체를 찾아 먹는다. 국외에서는 유럽 남부, 중앙아시아, 티베트, 몽골, 중국 북동부에 산다.

points.en: bare grey-brown skin on the head
plumage fades to brown with age

art.subject: Cinereous Vulture (Aegypius monachus), adult, as seen in Korean winter fields from November to March: plumage dark chocolate-brown all over, the body and wing coverts slightly browner than the blackish flight feathers; a loose ruff of long dark brown feathers at the base of the neck. Head covered with short pale brownish down on the crown, a blackish mask around the eye and down the cheeks and throat, and bare bluish-grey skin on the hindneck and sides of the neck. Bill massive and deeply hooked, dark horn-black, with a pale bluish-mauve cere. Eye dark brown.
art.pose: soaring on a thermal with wings held still
art.scene: Korean winter farmland near the northern border (Cheorwon–Paju area): frozen harvested rice paddies with patches of snow, a loose flock of vultures standing on the ground, bare low hills under a pale winter sky; no people, buildings or text
views: adult, side view standing on the ground: dark chocolate-brown body, neck ruff, pale brownish crown with blackish face mask, bare bluish-grey skin on the neck, massive hooked bill with a pale bluish cere
adult, soaring seen from below: very long, broad, parallel-edged wings held flat with deep fingers, uniformly dark underwing and body, short wedge-shaped tail, small head barely projecting
juvenile (first winter), side view standing: plumage blacker and more uniform than the adult, head covered with blackish down, pinkish cere and bare skin at the base of the bill
art.build: Huge vulture, 100–110cm, by far the largest raptor in Korea and much bigger than any eagle there; on the ground bulky and hunched, often standing with the head sunk into the ruff. Head small relative to the body; bill very deep and heavy, about as long as the head. At rest the long wings reach about the tail tip. Tail short and slightly wedge-shaped. Soars and glides for long periods on very long, broad, parallel-edged wings held flat or with the hand slightly drooped, with seven deeply fingered primaries and the head barely projecting; uniformly dark from below.
avoid: Do not paint a pale downy neck ruff or a sandy-buff body — that is a griffon vulture, not this species.
Do not paint a red, wrinkled bare head like a New World vulture.
Do not paint pale or white underwing coverts or a pale tail; the bird is dark all over.
Do not paint a long tail or narrow, eagle-like wings.
